open_obligations: Check whether Smit et al.'s Society of Minds matches Du et al.'s prompts and rounds.
Note the datasets differ (medical and reasoning QA versus arithmetic, GSM8K, biographies).
in.other_title: No protocol dominates all datasets; debate does not win on reasoning datasets
in.rationale: Du et al. report multi-agent debate improves reasoning and factuality over single-agent baselines. Smit et al. report no protocol dominates on seven QA datasets, Medprompt performs best overall, and the debating protocols (Society of Minds, Multi-Persona, ChatEval) do not outperform others on the reasoning datasets; Smit et al. include self-consistency and ensembling baselines that Du et al. do not.
in.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether multi-agent debate reliably improves LLM reasoning and factuality over other prompting strategies

text: The paper proposes that multiple instances of a language model propose answers and then debate their responses and reasoning over several rounds until they reach a common final answer. The authors report that this improves mathematical and strategic reasoning on several tasks and improves factual validity, reducing hallucinated answers, using only black-box access and the same prompts across tasks.
title: Multiagent debate between LLM instances improves reasoning and factual accuracy
